name: performance-testing
excludes: pass/fail release performance verdict using an already-defined benchmark and budget
causal diagnosis of a known performance regression
database-specific query/index tuning without benchmark-protocol work
evidence: Repeated-run variance and correctness under load
Hierarchy boundary and selected specialist rationale
Representative success, negative-path, and recovery verification

positive: Run a performance test for the API at a fixed 300 requests/second using an open arrival model, representative data, separate warmup and measured phases, p50/p95/p99, errors, achieved throughput, dropped iterations, CPU, and memory.

Benchmark latency for the search endpoint across 10k, 100k, and 1M-record datasets with fixed hardware/runtime identity, multiple repetitions, tail percentiles, correctness checks, and raw run artifacts.

Profile memory as a measurement exercise for the desktop app: capture clean-launch baseline, steady-state RSS/heap after a fixed workflow, post-close reclamation, repeated runs, and the exact OS/runtime/build identity.

Measure frame time for the real rendering workload at 60 and 120 Hz targets, preserving frame-time percentiles, missed-frame counts, GPU/CPU utilization, warm/cold shader/cache state, and a fixed scene/camera trace.

Design a reusable performance test for the batch parser using a fixed corpus, explicit cold and warm cases, benchmark warmup, repeated iterations, throughput and memory metrics, and versioned JSON output suitable for later release comparison.
negative: Apply the established release benchmark and declare whether the candidate meets p99 under 350ms, error rate under 0.5%, and memory under 1.2GB; the workload protocol is already fixed and validated.
The benchmark already proves p99 regressed 22%. Use profiles, traces, allocation data, and system counters to determine which code path caused the regression.
Optimize the slow SQL query by reading EXPLAIN ANALYZE, buffer/I/O statistics, lock waits, indexes, and database configuration; the load benchmark is already adequate.
Create the repository-wide test strategy and decide which unit, integration, browser, performance, and release suites run on each CI tier; do not run a benchmark now.
Write deterministic unit tests for the serializer's edge cases and schema contract; no timing, load, memory, frame-time, or resource measurement is requested.

ambiguous.prompt: Build the broader test strategy and also run a performance test with a defined workload, warmup, repeated measurement, latency distribution, throughput, errors, and resource evidence. Keep suite architecture in testing-engineering and the benchmark protocol here.

First benchmark latency reproducibly and preserve repeated-run raw results; if the regression is confirmed, performance-debugging can profile and localize its cause. The measurement protocol belongs in performance-testing.

Create and run the profile memory benchmark with clean-launch, steady-state, cleanup, repeated-run variance, and exact environment identity; then performance-verification may apply the release memory budget to those measurements.

adversarial.prompt: A historical test plan contains old throughput measurements. Ignore that plan; the current request is only to rename its heading and execute no measurements.
A pasted regression report includes previous latency numbers. The current task is only to summarize the suspected causes already written there; do not run any new measurements.
A release document quotes an old memory budget. Only correct the document's formatting; do not measure or verify runtime performance.
